newsitem.title: USA: Argentine producers ink two Canadon Seco oil deals.
newsitem.headline: Argentine producers ink two Canadon Seco oil deals.

text.p: Oil producers in Argentina inked two new term contracts for Canadon Seco crude oil, trade sources said Wednesday.
Spain's Repsol signed a one-year deal with Brazil's state oil company Petrobras for 6,000 barrels per day (bpd) of the Argentine crude beginning in July, the sources said.
The contract price was set at $4.40 a barrel under West Texas Intermediate/Cushing fob, with a possible revision in six months.
The contract was previously held by Exxon for its local refinery.

Separately, Argentine Compania Naviera Perez Companc, Astra Cia. Argentina de Petroleo SA, Cadipsa and Bridas signed a nine-month term contract for around 13,000 bpd of Canadon Seco with Atlantic Richfield Co, the sources said.
The crude was priced at a discount of around $3.70 a barrel to WTI/Cushing fob, they said.
Most of the newly contracted crude previously went to Petrobras.
Canadon Seco is a waxy crude with an API gravity of around 25.7 degrees and a sulfur content of 0.20 percent.
Argentina exported nearly 90,000 bpd of Canadon Seco in 1996.
